title: Reverse a Sequence Using a Stack
description: Read N integers, push them onto a stack, then print them in reverse order by popping the stack.
input_format: First N (1 ≤ N ≤ 1000), followed by N integers.
output_format: Print the values in reverse order, separated by single spaces.

starter_code.Python:
n = int(input())
values = list(map(int, input().split()))
stack = []
for value in values[:n]:
    stack.append(value)
reversed_values = []
while stack:
    reversed_values.append(str(stack.pop()))
print(" ".join(reversed_values))

learning_content.title: Stacks and last-in, first-out
learning_content.intro: A stack is a linear data structure that follows last-in, first-out (LIFO). The most recently pushed value is the first value popped.
points: Push each value onto the stack in input order.
Append each popped value to the output.
Print the values in the order they were popped.
learning_content.note: Each value is pushed once and popped once.

quiz.question: A stack receives 2, then 5, then 7. Which value is popped first?

options.feedback: 2 was pushed first and is at the bottom of the stack.
5 is below 7, so it is not popped first.
7 was pushed last, so it is on top and is popped first.

options.label: All three at once
options.feedback: A standard stack pop removes one top element at a time.

quiz.explanation: Stacks use LIFO: last in, first out.
